children: Hua Medicine reported that HMS1005 was generally well tolerated and glucose-control measures improved over 14 days in a U.S. Phase 1b trial enrolling 48 patients across six dose cohorts. No prior-period comparison was provided.
Early pharmacodynamic evidence supports further development, but the short treatment period does not establish durable efficacy.
The small early-stage study limits conclusions about efficacy and safety.
Once-daily doses ranged from 123 mg to 492 mg
The tested range informs dose selection for future studies; no comparative dose-response results were provided.
Tolerability supports continued testing, but larger and longer trials are needed to characterize safety.
FDA discussions planned; longer studies expected
The next catalyst is a defined development path and longer-term efficacy and safety data.

This is an early-stage clinical update building on Phase 1a findings and Hua Medicine's experience with dorzagliatin. The next catalysts are FDA discussions and longer studies evaluating selected once-daily doses, including effects on HbA1c and other glycemic measures.
